name: MUSICIAN Audio Technology
_terms_not_concluded: No terms page found on musician-audio.com, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding no prohibition. Measured 2026-11-25: every footer link on both language versions read, EVERY live col.jsp page enumerated and swept for copyright, reproduc, reprint, all rights, intellectual propert, without permission, 版权, 禁止, 转载 and 未经, with the footer the only hit. robots.txt is 404 on both hosts. Footers: « ©2026 musician copyright » and « ©2026 musician 版权所有 ». Records written because nothing forbidding was found.
_the_site_is_HTTP_ONLY: No HTTPS listener exists on either host, so a fetcher that upgrades to HTTPS cannot reach this maker at all - everything was read with curl, which also needs --compressed because the server returns gzip regardless of Accept-Encoding. Worth recording as a reachability fact rather than a refusal: the brand would have looked unreachable to any ordinary tool.
_musicianaudio_com_is_a_PARKED_DOMAIN_an: A trap that would have manufactured a refusal. musicianaudio.com is a GoDaddy parked domain - nameservers NS39/NS40.DOMAINCONTROL.COM, a 114-byte JavaScript redirect to /lander, a sitemap holding that one URL - and it serves a plausible robots.txt with « LLM-Policy: /llms.txt », whose llms.txt reads « Disallow-Training: / ». That belongs to the PARKING SERVICE. Recording it as MUSICIAN's policy would have invented a maker's refusal out of a registrar's default page, and it is the exact inverse of the Shopify robots.txt injection: there a platform spoke TO the agent, here a platform speaks FOR the maker. musicianhifi.com is also not the maker - a Hong Kong dealer on Wix.
_a_template_block_on_NINE_pages_includin: One Chinese block headed « Aquarius » is injected into the template and appears identically on nine pages, among them Gemini, a Class-AB power amplifier, and Knight I V2, a pair of loudspeakers - neither of which contains a converter. So nothing in it is attributable to any model, and that matters because it carries an NOS button legend and a « 每级滤波具32Bit输入解析度 » figure that would otherwise have landed on five records. It does settle the vocabulary question, though: its « NOS:超取样开/关按键，指示灯灭为超取样；指示灯亮原采样率；» is an oversampling on/off button, so NOS here means non-oversampling, corroborated by the English « Non-Oversampling NOS / Oversampling OS » on the product pages themselves.
_no_converter_part_number_exists_anywher: Swept every live page for ES9, AK4, PCM17, PCM18, CS43, AD19, sabre and burr: zero hits. The only parts named are STM32F446 (USB), an ALTERA FPGA (control and DSP) and LT1763/LT3045 (regulators). Consistent with discrete R-2R throughout, and recorded as an absence rather than as a chip. No BNC socket is mentioned anywhere either - clock connections exist on Phoenix, Leo, Pisces III and Taurus but none is described as BNC and none carries audio.
_not_converters_and_not_recorded: Phoenix, Leo and Pisces III are digital interfaces - digital in, digital out - so their high rates are OUTPUT ceilings and merging them with DAC input figures would be an error. Monoceros III is a preamplifier, Andromeda a headphone amplifier whose volume is « alpis potentiometer » (a potentiometer, not a resistor ladder, so no confusion with R-2R arises), Gemini a Class-AB power amplifier whose « Fully Discrete » describes no converter at all, and Knight I V2 a pair of loudspeakers.
_still_to_harvest: The maker publishes its own PDF manuals at col.jsp?id=105, including « User's Manual for PEGASUS III.pdf », « User's Manual for Draco III.pdf » and « User's Manual for Delphinus.pdf ». Those three models' records are the thin ones - Pegasus III and Draco III have no NOS statement in page text and Delphinus has no rate at all - and the manuals would very likely settle all of it as extractable text. The flagship pages are otherwise single JPEGs of 10.3 MB and 8.8 MB, from which nothing was read.
_merged_from_a_duplicate_file: musician-audio-technology.json held the same maker under id musician_audio_technology and was deleted on 2026-11-25. The six records carry brand « musician », so this file survives. Keys carried over: none, it held nothing new. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE DAY that a script writing a brand note invented a second file because it guessed the filename instead of looking it up - after Cambridge Audio and Cyrus. The first two were found by the guard added that morning; this one was caught by it before any commit, which is the whole point of the guard and the reason it was made an error rather than a warning. The real defect is upstream: a helper that falls back to CREATING a brand file when it cannot find one should instead refuse and say which filenames it tried.
